cited_details.statement: The newly emerging text-based person search task aims at retrieving a target pedestrian by a query in natural language with a fine-grained description of a pedestrian https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/56e3758cd9acc97f41ed3dbefd66fd76f238e4fb.

Text-based person search is more applicable in reality because it does not require an image or video query of a pedestrian, unlike image- or video-based person search such as person re-identification https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/56e3758cd9acc97f41ed3dbefd66fd76f238e4fb.

Person Search (PS) has become a major research field because of its importance in the community and its significance in video surveillance for tracking lost people, re-identification, and person verification https://doi.org/10.1016/j.imavis.2020.103970.

Deep learning has shown incredible performance in person re-identification and search, with convolutional neural networks achieving breakthrough performance and extracting useful patterns and characteristics https://doi.org/10.1016/j.imavis.2020.103970.
Existing person re-identification benchmarks and methods mainly focus on matching cropped pedestrian images between queries and candidates https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.01850.
However, real-world scenarios lack pedestrian bounding-box annotations, so the target person must be found directly from whole scene images http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~xgwang/PS/dataset.html.

To close this gap, an end-to-end deep learning framework jointly handles pedestrian detection and person re-identification rather than treating them as two separate tasks http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~xgwang/PS/dataset.html.
A random sampling softmax loss is proposed to train the model effectively under the supervision of sparse and unbalanced labels http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~xgwang/PS/dataset.html.
Joint Detection and Identification Feature Learning investigates pedestrian detection and matching simultaneously within a single network for person search https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.01850.

Person re-identification faces challenging issues including low resolution, pose variation, background clutter, occlusion, viewpoints, and low illumination that researchers seek to address https://doi.org/10.1016/j.imavis.2020.103970.

A deep adversarial graph attention convolution network, called A-GANet, exploits both textual and visual scene graphs consisting of object properties and relationships from text queries and gallery images of pedestrians https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/56e3758cd9acc97f41ed3dbefd66fd76f238e4fb.

A-GANet consists of an image graph attention network, a text graph attention network, and an adversarial learning module https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/56e3758cd9acc97f41ed3dbefd66fd76f238e4fb.

A-GANet learns a joint textual-visual latent feature space in an adversarial learning manner, bridging the modality gap and facilitating pedestrian matching https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/56e3758cd9acc97f41ed3dbefd66fd76f238e4fb.

A semantic-aligned feature representation method for text-based person search notes that global-matching methods cannot effectively explore the distinctive local details of samples that benefit performance https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.06714.

Adversarial representation learning for text-to-image matching targets computer vision applications such as image captioning, visual question answering, and person search by learning discriminative feature representations for both images and text https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10534.
A natural language person search approach based on deep reinforcement learning crops candidate person images to the same size as the query target before matching https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.00365.

An attention-based natural language person retrieval method addresses challenges such as low resolution, deformation, and occlusion when recognizing persons from textual queries https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.08923.

An Asymmetric Cross-Scale Alignment method has been proposed for text-based person search to align cross-modal features across scales https://cronfa.swan.ac.uk/Record/cronfa62251/Download/62251__26475__9db5b190500e40af9bfe9f45e66bbb4f.pdf.

A study on text-based person search with limited data investigates the setting where annotated text-image pairs are scarce during training https://www.bmva-archive.org.uk/bmvc/2021/assets/papers/0044.pdf.

Open research problems in image-based person search include developing new frameworks that demand substantial effort, hard work, and computation cost to acquire excellent results https://doi.org/10.1016/j.imavis.2020.103970.
Person search benchmarks remain limited in scale, and the samples are collected from a few fixed camera views http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~xgwang/PS/dataset.html.
For text-based approaches, handling low resolution, deformation, and occlusion remains difficult when matching pedestrians from natural language descriptions https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.08923.
